subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Left hand pain and numbness for a few months.
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 45 years old, and I'm here because my left hand has been bothering me with pain and numbness for a few months now. It's been worse at night, and sometimes I wake up with my hand feeling asleep and have to shake it out to get the feeling back. Doctor: Can you describe the exact location of the pain and numbness in your left hand? Have you noticed any weakness or difficulty with fine motor tasks, such as gripping objects or typing? Have you experienced similar symptoms in other parts of your body? Patient: The pain and numbness are mainly in my left wrist and hand, and it seems to affect all my fingers, but I notice it more in my thumb and pointer finger. I've had some weakness in my left hand, and I do drop things sometimes because I have a hard time feeling them. I haven't had any similar symptoms in other parts of my body. Doctor: Have you undergone any previous neurological or musculoskeletal evaluations for this condition? If so, what were the findings or diagnoses? Patient: No, I haven't had any previous neurological or musculoskeletal evaluations for this condition. I just noticed the symptoms a few months ago and haven't seen a doctor about it before today. Doctor: Could you describe any activities or positions that seem to aggravate or relieve your symptoms? Additionally, have you noticed any tingling, burning, or electric shock-like sensations in your left hand? Patient: The symptoms seem to get worse at night, and I usually wake up with my hand feeling asleep. I have to shake it out to get the feeling back. I also feel a little jolt or zing in my fingertips when the doctor tapped on my wrist. It's not something that happens all the time, but it does happen occasionally. Doctor: Could you please describe the specific location of the tingling or electric shock-like sensations in your fingertips, and have you noticed any patterns or triggers for these sensations? Patient: The tingling
